3|# Ponytail
4|
5|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.
6|
7|Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.
8|
9|## Before you write
10|
11|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.
12|
13|## The smallest complete change
14|
15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|
17|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
18|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
19|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
20|4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
21|5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
22|6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.
23|
24|- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
25|- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
26|- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
27|- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
28|- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
29|- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
30|- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
31|- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
32|- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
33|
34|Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.

73|## Lectoria rules
74|
75|- The text unit is the scene, not the paragraph or chapter.
76|- Paragraph ids are global, like `c12p34`.
77|- The emotion taxonomy has 8 ASCII ids: calma, alegria, tristeza, suspenso, misterio, aventura, combate, asombro. 79|- Public-domain books only.
80|- Images follow the book text and the W. W. Denslow 1900 illustrations: silver shoes, nothing from the 1939 MGM film.
81|- Never copy code from github.com/martinmw13/lectoria.
82|- Test with the cheapest models (Contributor). Use Standard for the final pass and the public chat.

84|## Product rules
85|
86|Owner decisions. Short and binding.
87|
88|- Desktop first. No mobile or iOS work now.
89|- The reader shows one scene at a time. Sub-pages split long scenes by length only. Music cues run on scene entry.
90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion.
91|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.
92|- `book.json` is frozen with a `textVersion` hash. Every cache key includes it.
93|- Scenes cover each chapter's paragraphs with no gaps and no overlaps. No scene crosses a chapter boundary. Scenes split at strong sequential emotion shifts; blends stay in the vector.
94|- Emotions are distributions. Each scene stores the full Jev probability vector over the 8 ids, plus `intensity` (0 to 1) and `tempo` (energy, 0 to 1). The Muse override on low confidence edits the vector and records that it did. It never swaps in a single label.
95|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. Each track is a weighted blend of emotions and carries an emotion vector plus intensity and tempo. The proposed way to pick the blends: cluster the Oz scene vectors and use the centroids as track prompts.
96|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
97|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.
98|- MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC. The hackathon demo is non-commercial. The generated tracks must say so in their README.
99|- Chat is low priority and simple. The context is the book text up to the reader's current position. The book prefix goes first and the question goes last, so readers share the prompt cache. Oz is about 55k tokens.
100|- The chat system prompt answers only from the provided text. It refuses knowledge beyond it, even if the model knows the book.
101|- A spoiler mode toggle is for readers who finished the book. It sends the whole text so they can ask about later events. No live Glimmer spoiler guard. No per-chapter summaries for chat. Citing passages is optional.
102|- Glimmer (open weights) keeps a pipeline role. Current decision: it writes the per-scene "why this music" explanation shown in the Developer View.
103|- Spikes come before feature code. Throwaway scripts in `scripts/spikes/` measure Muse Image (response format, latency, Denslow-style prompt), Meta `json_schema` structured output, and the Jev vector on a few Oz scenes. Results go to `docs/spikes.md`.
104|- Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars. Reserve with Redis `INCRBY` before each model call and refund with `DECRBY` after. Reserve per call, including retries.
105|- The server clamps every model tool argument. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
106|- The CSP allows `challenges.cloudflare.com` (script and frame) and `*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com` (images).
107|- The "Picture this" cache key is the book plus the paragraph where the selection starts plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`. Never generate the same image twice for one paragraph. The prompt is built from that paragraph plus scene context.
108|- The "Picture scene" cache key is the book plus the scene id plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion`.

112|## Security rules
113|
114|Summary. The full rules live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

13|# Ponytail
14|
15|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.

19|## Before you write
20|
21|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.

23|## The smallest complete change
24|
25|Take the first option that fully works:
26|
27|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
28|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
29|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.

9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.

21|covered zero or two times. The `resplit` pipeline step (after
22|`classify`, before `cluster`) cuts candidate scenes into ~100 to 160

1|# Task 11: re-split scenes at strong sequential emotion shifts
2|
3|A scene must hold one mood, since music changes only at scene
4|boundaries. Oz has 133 scenes; 28 have top final probability below
5|0.5 and 17 have a top-2 gap below 0.15, so some scenes mix moods
6|(calm, then the cyclone).
7|
8|New pipeline step `resplit` runs after `classify` and before
9|`cluster`. It reads book.json and analysis.json and rewrites
10|scenes.json and analysis.json. A scene is a candidate when it has
11|more than 350 words, a top probability below 0.5, or a top-2 gap
12|below 0.15. Scenes under 240 words never split, and scenes with no
13|vector stay as they are.
14|
15|Each candidate is cut into consecutive windows of whole paragraphs,
16|about 100 to 160 words each, and each window is classified with the
17|Jev client. The pure rule in `core/resplit.ts` scores each boundary:
18|with L and R the word-weighted mean vectors left and right, and a
19|and b their top emotions, the margin is min(L[a]-L[b], R[b]-R[a])
20|when a and b differ. Each side must hold at least 120 words, and a
21|one-window spike does not count as persistence.
22|
23|A margin at or above 0.30 splits at once. A margin from 0.15 to 0.30
24|asks Muse, which sees two paragraphs each side plus both vectors and
25|answers split or not with a reason. Below 0.15 nothing splits.
26|Target is 5 to 30 splits on Oz.
27|
28|The first part keeps the scene id so old links keep working; later
29|parts add a letter suffix (`c5s2b`, `c5s2c`). One Meta call per split
30|scene writes titles, summaries, and characters; each part is
31|re-classified with the standard classify path. Coverage validation
32|runs before writing. Provenance lands under `provenance.resplit`,

34|keeps its "Picture scene" image key; no such image is live yet.

1|# Contracts
2|
3|Music generation must never block the reader. Each module below owns one
4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is
5|`core <- server` and `core <- app`. Server and client components never
6|import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client
7|files never do.
8|
9|## Book data
10|
11|`data/books/oz/book.json` holds the frozen text: id, title, author,
12|`textVersion` hash, chapters with `start_n` and `end_n`, and paragraphs
13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source
14|the reader consumes: the same scenes plus Jev vectors, the Muse
15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times. The `resplit` pipeline step (after
22|`classify`, before `cluster`) cuts candidate scenes into ~100 to 160
23|word windows, classifies each window with Jev, and splits at the
24|strongest persistent dominant-emotion shift (auto at margin 0.30,
25|Muse decides 0.15 to 0.30, none below). The first part keeps the
26|scene id with letter-suffixed later parts; provenance lands under
27|`provenance.resplit` in `analysis.json`.
28|
29|## Scene reader
30|
31|One static route per scene (`app/leer/[sceneId]`, `dynamicParams`
32|false); `/` redirects to the first scene. The layout mounts the music
33|container once and passes slim metadata for all scenes: id, chapter,
34|and emotion triple only. Each scene page builds its view with
35|`buildSceneView` and ships only that scene's text, its chapter title,
36|and neighbor ids. Sub-pages come from `paginateScene`, which closes a
37|page when the next paragraph would pass 250 words or the line budget
38|(`FIRST_PAGE_LINES` 16 on page one, `LINES_PER_PAGE` 17 after, each
39|paragraph costing `ceil(chars / CHARS_PER_LINE)` lines with
40|`CHARS_PER_LINE` 68), split at paragraph boundaries. The pager moves sub-pages in client state and
41|pushes routes with `router.push`, never `<Link>`; going back lands on
42|the previous scene's last sub-page through a one-shot client flag, never
43|a URL param, so prerendered pages stay static. The client never
44|receives other scenes' text, titles, or summaries. The progress line
45|reads `Chapter 1 · The Cyclone`, a spaced separator, then `Scene 1 of 4
46|· Page 1 of 3` as two spans on one line. Book type is 1.1875rem / 1.7
47|with no paragraph gaps and a 1.5em first-line indent on following
48|paragraphs. The word budget stays the upper bound and the line budget
49|keeps every sub-page inside 1280×800 without scroll.
50|
51|## Music library
52|
53|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 3, fetched
54|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
55|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
56|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so. A version 2
57|manifest migrates inline to one implicit `default` soundtrack of style
58|`orchestral`.
59|
60|`MusicManifest = { version, styles, soundtracks, tracks, playlists }`.
61|`StyleInfo = { id, name }` where `id` is a lowercase slug and `name` is
62|the display name. `Soundtrack = { id, name, style }` plus
63|optional `credit`. `Track = { id, src, title, emotion, vector,
64|intensity, tempo, durationSec, soundtrack, style }` plus optional
65|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
66|loop), `endSec` (default the media end, where the track stops or loops),
67|`gainDb` (default 0, a loudness trim in dB, in -24..12),
68|`loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
69|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
70|`sourceUrl` (https only). `durationSec` is the playable length: the
71|segment end (or the file end) minus `startSec`. `startSec` and `endSec`
72|are absolute media times with `startSec < endSec`; `endSec` stays within
73|`startSec + durationSec`. The player scales volume by the track gain and
74|ends or loops at `effectiveEnd`, the earlier of `endSec` and the loaded
75|media end. `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
76|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
77|entries in 0..1. Every track names a soundtrack id, every track style
78|matches its soundtrack style, and every style is a listed style id.
79|`core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions,
80|duplicate ids, unknown soundtrack or style ids, style mismatches,
81|missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range numbers,
82|a negative `startSec`, a bad `gainDb` or `endSec`, unknown `source`
83|values, a non-boolean
84|`playlistOnly`, and any `src`
85|that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. Unknown fields stay
86|ignored. A soundtrack with no
87|tracks parses. The reader calls it on every fetch, so a bad drop-in
88|fails loudly in dev. Remote audio lives on one Blob store, so
89|`media-src` in `next.config.ts` lists exactly
90|`https://3vuhzq2wmortnuxj.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`. Build the
91|manifest with `npm run build:music data/music/labels.json
92|data/music/library.json --out public/music/manifest.json`, which runs
93|`pipeline/labels-to-manifest.ts` and validates the result before
94|writing.
95|
96|`Track.playlistOnly` defaults to false. A true value marks a playlist
97|only track: it still names a soundtrack and style, but no emotion pick
98|ever returns it. `MusicManifest.playlists` holds
99|`Playlist = { id, label, trackIds }` entries, most notably
100|`just-play-chopin`. A missing key parses as an empty list, and a v2
101|migration gives an empty list. Parse rejects duplicate playlist ids,
102|empty labels, non-array `trackIds`, and any `trackIds` entry that names
103|no track, with the playlist and the id in the message.
104|
105|## Selection
106|
107|`MusicSelection = { style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick.
108|There is one mode only. Every scheduled select ranges over all tracks in
109|the current style and draws among the tracks with the scene emotion (or
110|the best same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within
111|`randomTolerance` (0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when
112|it is eligible, and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. The style is
113|the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The default style is
114|the first listed style with tracks; a stored style with tracks wins. The
115|session persists `{ style, volume, muted }` in localStorage under
116|`lectoria.music.v1`. Old values with `mode` or `soundtrackId` load by
117|`style` alone and ignore unknown fields; a stored object without
118|`volume` or `muted` loads `volume: null` and `muted: false`. A bad
119|`volume` (not a finite number in 0..1) loads null and the player starts
120|at 0.8; a bad `muted` loads false. A stored style with no tracks falls
121|back to the default. Storage exceptions never break playback. Dwell
122|and min-track rules hold. The core never calls `Math.random`; the
123|reader injects it and tests pass a seeded stub.
124|
125|## Next track and style change
126|
127|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order across the whole
128|style, wrapping and skipping the current, then the best same-style track
129|overall when the emotion is missing. A null scene cycles the style set
130|in id order. One track or none gives null.
131|
132|`requestStyleChange` picks the best match for the scene in the new style
133|by score. It never crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once
134|with the normal crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
135|mix toggle and no soundtrack-change button.
136|
137|## Playlist mode
138|
139|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
140|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
141|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
142|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
143|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
144|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
145|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
146|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
147|restored selection. The playlist is never persisted, so a reload returns
148|to emotion mode. The style selector stays disabled while it is on, and
149|the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
150|
151|## Similarity and config
152|
153|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
154|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
155|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
156|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
157|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
158|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
159|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
160|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
161|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
162|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `dwellSec` (20),
163|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5), `minTrackSec` (45), `crossfadeSec` (3), and
164|`randomTolerance` (0.05). Everything else reads from it. Ranking ties go
165|to the lower track id. Route entries use `sceneEntryDwellSec` as the
166|dwell override; scoring and overrides are unchanged.
167|
168|## Selection scheduler
169|
170|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
171|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
172|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
173|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
174|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
175|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
176|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
177|with the scene it belongs to.
178|
179|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
180|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
181|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
182|becomes active and the override clears. Then a scheduled select draws
183|among the in-style tracks within `randomTolerance` of the best score,
184|keeping the current track when it is eligible, and switches to the
185|drawn track only once the current track played `minTrackSec`. A tick
186|passes the active scene back through the same draw, so a hold from
187|`minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a skip override stands: ticks
188|return no change while it is set, and only a new scene promotion
189|clears it. A switch reports the normal crossfade length (3 s, 0 s for
190|the first track ever). The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
191|after that, dwell and the draw apply with the override track as the
192|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
193|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
194|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
195|skip override.
196|
197|## Player
198|
199|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, `replayNonce`, the fade length for
200|the latest switch, `canPrev`/`canSkip` with their handlers, volume and
201|mute with their handlers, the style list with the current style and its
202|handler, the end-of-track handler, and the playlist props
203|(`playlistOn`, `playlistLabel`, `onTogglePlaylist`,
204|`controlsDisabled`). It owns two `audio`
205|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
206|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
207|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
208|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
209|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
210|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
211|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
212|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
213|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
214|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
215|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
216|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
217|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
218|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
219|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
220|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
221|
222|The bar is one sticky row, 56 px tall: the `Lectoria` wordmark left,
223|the player centre, the Chopin button and the source icon link right.
224|The inner row is centered with 24 px side padding, one bottom hairline
225|in the border token, and nothing touching the viewport edges. The inner
226|max-width is 56rem, wider than the 65ch book column on purpose so the
227|full now-playing line fits at 1280 px. The player holds Previous,
228|Play/Pause, Next, the now-playing line (flexible space, `min-width`

261|`core/music-credit.ts` builds the line as a pure function with tests,

263|`core/music-history.ts` is the bounded history stack and

266|## Image api
